related_questions.question: What is the ICD-10 code for illness?

text_blocks.snippet: The ICD-10 code for a general, unspecified illness is R69. This code is used when a patient's illness is not further specified or diagnosed. The ICD-10-CM (Clinical Modification) is used in the United States to code and classify medical diagnoses.
Key points about ICD-10 code R69:

list.snippet: Unspecified illness: R69 is used when the specific cause or type of illness is not documented or known.
Reimbursement: This code can be used for reimbursement purposes.
Part of a larger system: R69 is part of the broader ICD-10-CM system, which is used to classify diseases, symptoms, and other health-related conditions.
You can find more details about ICD-10 codes on the CDC website or the AAPC website.
The ICD-10-CM is managed by the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS).
The WHO (World Health Organization) publishes the base version of the ICD-10, which you can find on their website.
